subtitle: Where Dusty Roads Met Silver Fish

panels.shot: sweeping bird's-eye over an early city at a fork of two great roads
panels.action: Pradyota of Ujjain stands on a mud-brick terrace above a bustling crossroads, caravans from north and south converging as traders lift baskets and lead pack-animals through the smoky dawn of Avanti.

dialogue.text: Long before meridians and observatories, Ujjain under Pradyota was already a prize: a crossroads where two ancient roads, two faiths, and a kingdom’s fate met and bargained.

i18n.hi: देशांतर, वेधशालाओं से बहुत पहले, प्रद्योत के अधीन उज्जैन पहले ही इनाम था – दो राहों, दो मजहबों, एक राज्य की किस्मत का सौदा-घर।

panels.shot: wide map-like high angle fading into landscape panorama
panels.action: A parchment-like view of the subcontinent melts into real terrain: a dusty northern road snaking down past the Ganga plains and a southern track climbing through scrub and rocky hills toward the plateau of Malwa.

dialogue.text: The texts call it Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha: two long dirt arteries, one from the Ganga plains, one from the Deccan, pouring men, goods and stories toward a stony plateau called Malwa.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ इसे उत्तरापथ और दक्षिणापथ कहते हैं – दो लम्बी मिट्टी की नसें, एक गंगा के मैदानी इलाक़ों से, एक दक्कन से, जो आदमी, माल और किस्से बहा लाती थीं मलवा नाम के पथरीले पठार पर।

panels.shot: medium wide establishing shot of early Ujjain
panels.action: An early city of timber and mud-brick sprawls over a slight rise, smoke pillars from hearths, a moat-like ditch beyond, with carts entering through a simple wooden gate flanked by watchtowers.

dialogue.text: Here, at a bend of the Shipra, the Avanti kings raised Ujjain. Not yet stone towers and walls, but ditches, palisades, warehouses and markets—enough to tax, to shelter, to tempt caravans to stop.

i18n.hi: यहीं, शिप्रा के मोड़ पर, अव Anti के राजाओं ने उज्जैन बसाया – अभी न मीनारें, न पत्थर की दीवारें; बस खाइयाँ, बाँस-बाड़, गोदाम और बाज़ार – इतना कि कर लिया जा सके, पनाह दी जा सके, क़ाफ़िलों को रोका जा सके।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Pradyota in court courtyard
panels.action: Pradyota of Ujjain, in simple but rich cloth, sits on a low wooden throne under a canopy in an open courtyard, scribes with palm leaves beside him as traders and caravan leaders bow in front.

dialogue.text: Among those kings the Pali and Jain traditions remember Pradyota: sometimes fierce, sometimes just, always watchful, for a city at a crossroads grows rich, but also restless.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं राजाओं में से पाली और जैन परम्परा प्रद्योत को याद रखती है – कभी कठोर, कभी न्यायी, हमेशा चौकन्ना; क्योंकि दोराहे का नगर अमीर भी होता है, बैचैन भी।

panels.shot: tight medium on trader’s hands pouring coins before Pradyota
panels.action: A bearded trader kneels, pouring a small pile of worn silver punch-marked coins onto a low table before Pradyota; one coin bears a clear fish symbol under the lamplight.

dialogue.text: Later, in the earth, archaeologists would find their money: silver karshapanas punched with a little fish—distinctive marks of Avanti, silent witnesses to all these bargains.

i18n.hi: बाद में मिट्टी के नीचे पुरातत्वविदों ने उनकी दौलत पाई – चाँदी के कर्षापण, जिन पर छोटी मछली की ठप्पी थी – अव Anti की पहचान, इन सब सौदों के खामोश गवाह।

panels.shot: close-up on coin and trader’s weathered face
panels.action: Extreme close-up of the fish-marked coin in rough fingers, then the lined face of the trader glancing up anxiously toward Pradyota seated above.

dialogue.speaker: pradyota_and_the_ujjain_traders
dialogue.text: North or south, they pass our gates. Why should their coins slip by untaxed?

i18n.hi: उत्तर हों या दक्षिण, सब हमारे फाटक से गुजरते हैं; फिर उनके सिक्के कर के बिना कैसे फिसल जाएँ?

panels.shot: wide shot of bustling market inside Ujjain
panels.action: A teeming market street: bales of cotton and dyed cloth, jars of oil, iron tools, beads, and grain sacks, with cow-drawn carts and southern traders leading sturdy pack-bulls through the crowd as Pradyota watches from a balcony.

dialogue.text: Cotton and cloth from the Deccan, metals and salt from the north, grain from Malwa’s black soil—Ujjain took a slice of all, and in return offered safety, storage, and a ruler whose reach kept the roads mostly open.

i18n.hi: दक्कन से कपास और कपड़ा, उत्तर से धातु और नमक, मलवा की काली मिट्टी से अनाज – उज्जैन हर चीज़ से अपना हिस्सा लेता, और बदले में देता था राह की सुरक्षा, गोदाम, और ऐसा शासक जिसकी पकड़ से रास्ते ज़्यादातर खुले रहते।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot with monk visitor and Pradyota
panels.action: Inside a shaded hall, Pradyota sits cross-legged facing a visiting Buddhist monk with a travel staff, dusty feet, and a calm face; attentive courtiers linger behind.

dialogue.text: From the east, new wanderers appeared. Pali texts tell of Pradyota’s Avanti hearing of the Buddha, of monks debating whether to brave these rough western roads to carry their rules and ideas here.

i18n.hi: पूरब से नए भटकते आए; पाली ग्रंथ बताते हैं कि प्रद्योत की अव Anti ने बुद्ध का नाम सुना, और भिक्षु सोचते रहे कि नियम और विचार लेकर इन ऊबड़-पथरीले पश्चिमी रास्तों पर निकलें या नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of monk Sona Kutikanna on the road
panels.action: A lone monk, Sona Kutikanna, in a simple robe, walks along a stony path lined with scrub, carrying a bowl and staff, wind pushing dust around his feet as ox-carts pass him by.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya remembers Sona Kutikanna from Avanti: the monk whose harsh homeland—its cold, its sparse villages—forced the Buddha to bend some rules, so the Dhamma could travel even to this far crossroad.

i18n.hi: विनय में अव Anti के सोṇa कुटिकण्ण का ज़िक्र है – वह भिक्षु, जिसकी कठोर जन्मभूमि – सर्दी, विरले गाँव – ने बुद्ध को कुछ नियम ढीले करने पर मजबूर किया, ताकि धम्म इतनी दूर की चौपाल तक पहुँच सके।

panels.shot: quiet night scene in an Avanti village hut
panels.action: Inside a modest hut near Ujjain, Sona Kutikanna sits by a small fire with villagers, their faces lit by flame, as someone pours thin gruel into his bowl while outside the wind rattles the thatch.

dialogue.text: The texts note exceptions for Avanti: storing medicine a little longer, easing robes and food rules for lonely, cold places. Law met landscape, so that even in Pradyota’s rough country, discipline could survive.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ अव Anti के लिए छूट लिखते हैं – दवा थोड़ी देर और रखना, सूनसान, ठंडी जगहों के लिए कपड़ों और भिक्षा के नियम ढीले करना; यहाँ क़ानून ने ज़मीन से समझौता किया, ताकि प्रद्योत की उबड़-खाबड़ धरती में भी अनुशासन बचा रहे।

panels.shot: wide rural shot of Mahavira’s wanderings near Avanti
panels.action: Mahavira, in simple unclothed austerity suggested through careful drapery and posture, walks with a small group of Jain monks along a path skirting fields near Ujjain, farmers pausing to stare as he passes.

dialogue.text: Jain traditions in the Bhagavati Sutra place Mahavira in these parts too. They speak of Avanti rulers like Palaka, and of the Niganthas’ patient, barefoot circuits through Malwa’s villages and the outskirts of Ujjain.

i18n.hi: जैन परम्परा, भगवती सूत्र में, महावीर को भी इन इलाक़ों में रखती है; वे अव Anti के पालक जैसे शासकों का ज़िक्र करते हैं, और निगन्थों की धीमी, नंगे पाँव मलवा के गाँवों और उज्जैन की बाहरी बस्तियों की परिक्रमा का।

panels.shot: interior shot of Ujjain household with competing faiths
panels.action: Inside a trader’s home, a family listens as a Jain monk sits on a platform, while in a corner a Brahman recites from memory; Pradyota’s tax collector waits at the doorway counting coins in his hand.

dialogue.text: In such houses, loyalties were layered: ancestral rites, Jain vows, new Buddhist stories. For the king and his officials, what mattered first was that the house stood in Avanti, at Ujjain’s fork, under their tax.

i18n.hi: ऐसे घरों में निष्ठाएँ परत-दर-परत थीं – पुरखों की पूजा, जैन व्रत, नए बौद्ध किस्से; राजा और उसके मुलाज़िमों के लिए पहले बस इतना ज़रूरी था कि वह घर अव Anti में हो, उज्जैन के मोड़ पर, उनके कर के दायरे में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pradyota in council with map lines on ground
panels.action: Pradyota and his councillors sit in a circle, a simple map scratched in the dirt showing lines from north to south and east to west, with small pebbles marking forts and towns.

dialogue.text: Yet the crossroads gave danger with profit. To east lay rising Magadha; to west and south, other chiefs watched this node. King lists differ, but they agree: Avanti’s rulers fought, schemed, married, trying not to be swallowed.

i18n.hi: पर इस दोराहे ने फ़ायदे के साथ ख़तरा भी दिया – पूरब में उभरता मगध, पश्चिम और दक्षिण में दूसरे सरदार इस गाँठ को घूरते रहे; राजा-सूचियाँ भले बदलती हों, पर एक बात तय है – अव Anti के शासक लड़ते, साज़िशें करते, शादियाँ रचाते रहे, बस निगला जाने से बचने के लिए।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of Avanti soldiers on the road
panels.action: Lines of Avanti soldiers march along the road out of Ujjain, shields slung, spears up, as traders watch from the roadside and an anxious woman holds a child at the city gate.

dialogue.text: The Mahajanapada age was no quiet era. Avanti’s forces clashed with neighbours; tradition remembers battles with Magadha, truces born of fear and necessity, and a time when Pradyota’s line and rival dynasties eyed each other warily.

i18n.hi: महाजनपद का दौर कोई शान्त ज़माना न था – अव Anti की सेनाएँ पड़ोसियों से भिड़ीं; परम्परा मगध से युद्ध, डर और मजबूरी से बने संधि-समझौते, और वह वक़्त याद रखती है जब प्रद्योत की वंश-रेखा और उनके प्रतिद्वन्द्वी एक-दूसरे को तिरछी नज़र से देखते रहे।

panels.shot: ground-level shot along road showing caravans passing remains of skirmish
panels.action: Caravans creep past a field scarred with churned earth and abandoned spears, the soldiers gone; the traders look sideways but keep moving, oxen straining under loads.

dialogue.text: Each clash made traders wary. Yet they still came, because the roads met here, because turning back cost more than risk. That stubborn flow of carts and animals held Avanti’s economy together between wars.

i18n.hi: हर टक्कर से व्यापारी सहमते; फिर भी आते रहे – क्योंकि राहें यहीं मिलती थीं, क्योंकि लौट जाना जोखिम से ज़्यादा महँगा पड़ता; यही ज़िद्दी बैलगाड़ियाँ और जानवरों की कतारें युद्धों के बीच अव Anti की अर्थव्यवस्था को जोड़े रहीं।

panels.shot: archaeological cross-section style shot of Ujjain mound
panels.action: A cutaway view of a low mound beneath a modern-looking hint of city above, layers showing: broken pottery, a dark band of Northern Black Polished Ware shards, scattered fish-marked coins, then later debris.

dialogue.text: Much of that early Ujjain now lies buried under the living city. Archaeologists, scraping trenches in the twentieth century, met thin bands of Northern Black Polished Ware and coins, proof that an urban heart beat here by the sixth century BCE.

i18n.hi: उस पुराने उज्जैन का बहुत हिस्सा आज ज़िन्दा शहर के नीचे दबा है; बीसवीं सदी में जो पुरातत्वविद खाइयाँ खोदते गए, उन्हें पतली परतें उत्तरी काली चमकदार मृद्भांड की और सिक्कों की मिलीं – सबूत कि छठी सदी ईसा पूर्व तक यहाँ शहर का दिल धड़क रहा था।

panels.shot: introspective shot of a modern archaeologist in trench holding coin
panels.action: A modern archaeologist in a narrow trench, sweat on his brow, gently lifts a tarnished fish-marked coin from the soil, the bustling present-day town blurred in the background above.

dialogue.text: They could not uncover grand walls; too much life lay above. But a coin here, a floor there, a pit of ash and potsherds—together they traced the outline of Pradyota’s Ujjain, more modest than legend, yet unmistakably a crossroads city.

i18n.hi: वे कोई भव्य दीवार पूरी तरह न निकाल सके – ऊपर बहुत ज़िन्दगी बस चुकी थी; पर कहीं एक सिक्का, कहीं फर्श का टुकड़ा, कहीं राख और टूटे बर्तनों का गड्ढा – इन्हें जोड़कर उन्होंने प्रद्योत के उज्जैन की रेखा पकड़ी, किवदन्तियों से कम, पर साफ़-साफ़ दोराहे का नगर।

panels.shot: twilight wide shot of Pradyota on rampart overlooking roads
panels.action: At dusk, Pradyota stands alone on the earthen rampart of Ujjain, looking down where torches of caravans move like slow fireflies along both northern and southern roads.

dialogue.speaker: pradyota_and_the_ujjain_traders
dialogue.text: King, coin, monk, merchant—we all walk the same dust.

i18n.hi: राजा, सिक्का, भिक्षु, व्यापारी – सब एक ही धूल में चलते हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative aerial shot pulling up over crossroads fading into map
panels.action: The camera pulls up high above the criss-crossing roads by Ujjain, caravans shrinking to dots, the scene slowly blending into a simple map with Ujjain marked as a small but central node.

dialogue.text: Today, Avanti’s kings are names in lists and its streets lie under newer ones, but the choice they made—to seize a crossroads, tax its flow, and live by its risks—still whispers in every city that thrives where roads converge.

i18n.hi: आज अव Anti के राजा सूचियों में नाम भर रह गए हैं, और उसकी गलियाँ नई गलियों के नीचे दब गई हैं; पर उनका फैसला – दोराहा पकड़ना, उसकी धार पर कर लगाना और उसी जोखिम पर जीना – हर उस शहर में गूँजता है जो रास्तों के मिलन पर फलता है।

title_i18n.hi: अव Anti का दोराहे वाला नगर

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Dusty Roads Met Silver Fish
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ धूल भरे रास्ते मिले चाँदी सी मछलियों से
